claim_under_attack.claim_text: count_reactive_amine_hydrogens implements the published active-hydrogen convention correctly across amine classes.

does_not_close: EVALUATION_SIGNATURE_ABSENT (this is an AUDIT_ONLY science-validation replay, not a Phase-0 evaluation/review signature).

No repair to bridge.cc is made by this receipt -- this is a pure validation/falsification fire (W-FFI1), not a repair (R-) item. A follow-on repair item is warranted to special-case dicyandiamide (or the mechanistic melamine/heterocyclization pathway it undergoes) distinctly from pure catalytic guanidine/amidine accelerators.

Whether the correct fix counts DICY's active hydrogen as exactly 4 (simple textbook convention) or as an effective ~7 (some literature analyzes DICY's net epoxide uptake mechanistically, including nitrile and heterocyclization contributions, as higher than simple N-H counting) is left open for the repair item to resolve; this receipt only establishes that 0 is wrong.
Any change to bridge.cc, the R-N02/V-N02c receipts, or the master manifest (all read here but not modified).
The vinylogous-enaminone conjugation blind spot and ketimine self-exclusion side effect already disclosed as out-of-scope, non-refuting findings by V-N02c; not re-attacked here.
method: Authored a fresh, independent Rust binary crate (ffi1-verify, path-dependency on amphora-rdkit-ffi with feature=rdkit -- the REAL production FFI, not a reimplementation) that calls molecule_facts() on 14 pre-registered probe molecules spanning 10 amine classes. For each probe, an externally-published active-hydrogen count (and, for 11/14 probes, an externally-published molecular formula and molecular weight independently cross-checked against the toolkit's own computed formula/MW to confirm the SMILES encodes the intended structure) was pre-registered from a named published source -- Lee & Neville 1967 (Handbook of Epoxy Resins) curing-agent tables, vendor TDS/CAS-indexed data (Evonik/Huntsman IPDA, Union Carbide/Huntsman DETA/TETA/TEPA, Albemarle ETHACURE 100/DETDA), or -- for the single refuting probe -- an explicit quote from patent WO1993010168A1 'Bis-dicyandiamides as curing agents for epoxy resins' (1993). The amidine/guanidine class was deliberately split into two sub-classes: catalytic accelerators (guanidine, DPG) that R-N02/V-N02c already established should read 0 active hydrogen (never sold or dosed as stoichiometric hardeners), and dicyandiamide (DICY), which IS dosed near-stoichiometrically as a real production one-part epoxy/powder-coating hardener and for which WO1993010168A1 explicitly states: 'dicyandiamide (cyanoguanidine) has a defined degree of functionality of four, that is, it is capable of addition to four epoxide radicals.' This targets exactly the question R-N02's own receipt left explicitly open ('whether guanidine N-H is exactly zero in a quantitative AHEW sense is explicitly left open') with a citable external published answer, rather than re-testing R-N02/V-N02c's own internal-consistency probes.
objective: W-FFI1: validate amphora-rdkit-ffi/src/bridge.cc::count_reactive_amine_hydrogens against the PUBLISHED active-hydrogen convention (Lee & Neville 1967, Handbook of Epoxy Resins; AHEW = molecular weight / number of active amine hydrogens) across amine classes: primary / secondary / tertiary aliphatic, cycloaliphatic, aromatic (direct-N-aryl and aromatic-sulfone), hindered aromatic, amide, polyamine oligomer, and amidine/guanidine (both the catalytic-accelerator and the stoichiometric-hardener sub-classes). Claim under attack: amphora-rdkit-ffi/src/bridge.cc's count_reactive_amine_hydrogens implements the published active-hydrogen convention correctly across amine classes.
pre_registered_refute_criterion: CLAIM_REFUTED (for a given amine class) if the real production FFI's observed reactive_amine_hydrogen_count for ANY class member disagrees with that member's independently-published active-hydrogen count, PROVIDED the probe's own formula/MW independently cross-check confirms the SMILES encodes the structure the published source describes (ruling out a SMILES-authoring error as the source of any disagreement).

reproducibility.determinism_basis: no RNG, no wall clock, fixed hardcoded probe list, serde_json default BTreeMap (alphabetically sorted key) output; two independent `cargo run --release` process invocations produced byte-identical stdout (sha256 equal).
reproducibility.harness_binary_provenance: cargo run --release against amphora-rdkit-ffi (path dependency, feature=rdkit) compiled with cxx against the pinned RDKit 2026.03.2 prefix at /home/ubuntu/.local/share/amphora/rdkit-2026.03.2 (RDKIT_INCLUDE_DIR=.../include/rdkit, RDKIT_LIB_DIR=.../lib, BOOST_INCLUDE_DIR=.../include/boost); toolkit_provenance.exact_version_match=true recorded in every run.

refuting_probe.published_source: WO1993010168A1 'Bis-dicyandiamides as curing agents for epoxy resins' (1993), explicit quote: "dicyandiamide (cyanoguanidine) has a defined degree of functionality of four, that is, it is capable of addition to four epoxide radicals"; corroborated independently by multiple epoxy-curing patent/technical sources describing dicyandiamide as possessing four active hydrogens (with some literature noting apparent 3-active-hydrogen kinetic behavior, but never zero)
refuting_probe.root_cause: bridge.cc's is_amidine_or_guanidine_carbon exclusion (added by R-N02) categorically zeroes ANY amine nitrogen whose carbon neighbor carries a C=N double bond to any nitrogen, treating all amidine/guanidine-conjugated N-H identically regardless of whether the specific molecule functions in production as a weak non-nucleophilic catalytic accelerator (guanidine, DPG, DOTG -- correctly 0 per this same validation run) or as a genuine near-stoichiometric epoxy hardener (dicyandiamide) whose own published functionality is four, not zero. The rule conflates two chemically distinct real-world roles under one categorical structural exclusion.

rights_check: No new external data source opened or acquired. All probe molecules are CAS-identified public-domain chemical identities evaluated purely structurally via the already-licensed pinned RDKit backend. Published reference values are drawn from openly-searchable patent text (WO1993010168A1), CAS-indexed vendor technical-data-sheet facts (MW, formula), and the standard published Lee & Neville 1967 curing-agent convention already cited elsewhere in this repository; no quarantined or rights-restricted source was opened.
why: 13 of 14 pre-registered probes, spanning primary aliphatic, secondary aliphatic, tertiary aliphatic (zero-active-H control), cycloaliphatic, aromatic (direct-N-aryl and aromatic-sulfone), hindered aromatic, amide (exclusion-correctness), polyamine oligomer, and the amidine/guanidine catalytic-accelerator sub-class all reproduce their independently-published active-hydrogen counts exactly through the real production FFI, with every probe's own formula/MW independently confirmed against its published identity (ruling out SMILES-encoding error as an explanation either way). The amidine/guanidine STOICHIOMETRIC-HARDENER sub-class member, dicyandiamide (DICY), disagrees: the real FFI returns 0 active hydrogens, but patent WO1993010168A1 explicitly and unambiguously states dicyandiamide 'has a defined degree of functionality of four, that is, it is capable of addition to four epoxide radicals.' Since DICY is a real, commercially dominant, near-stoichiometrically-dosed one-part epoxy hardener in the exact coating-IP scope this portfolio targets, this is not an edge-case curiosity: bridge.cc's claim to implement the published active-hydrogen convention correctly ACROSS amine classes is REFUTED for the amidine/guanidine hardener sub-class. This closes, with a citable external published source, the exact question R-N02's own repair receipt left explicitly open.
